title: New Study Shows How Your Brain Changes at Four Key Ages: 9, 32, 66 and 83

sentences: The human brain has four distinct turning points where its structure changes, according to a study published in the journal Nature Communications, demonstrating that brain development is not as linear as you might think.
translations: 根据发表在《自然通讯》杂志上的一项研究，人类大脑有四个结构发生变化的明显转折点，这表明大脑发育并非像你想象的那样呈线性发展。

sentences: "It's easy to fall into this belief that there's a 'good' or 'bad' way for a brain to be structured," said lead study author Alexa Mousley at the University of Cambridge.
"What this study is emphasizing is the brain is expected to be doing something different at different ages."
translations: "人们很容易陷入这样一种观念，即大脑的结构存在'好'或'坏'的方式，"该研究的主要作者、剑桥大学的亚历克莎·穆斯利说。
"这项研究强调的是，大脑在不同年龄阶段应该做不同的事情。"

sentences: In the new study, Mousley and colleagues looked at around 4,000 scans from healthy people ages 0 to 90 and found four major times when the brain underwent developmental changes, around ages nine, 32, 66 and 83, dividing the lifespan into five distinct phases.
translations: 在这项新研究中，莫斯利及其同事查看了约4000名0至90岁健康人的脑部扫描结果，发现了大脑经历发育变化的四个主要时期，分别在大约9岁、32岁、66岁和83岁，从而将人的寿命划分为五个不同的阶段。

sentences: "It's yet another very nice example of how the brain and its global interactions change across the lifespan," said Seth Grant, a neuroscientist at The University of Edinburgh who wasn't involved in the new research.
"The message is, there is continuous change from birth until old age."
translations: "这是又一个很好的例子，展示了大脑及其全局互动如何在整个生命周期中发生变化，"爱丁堡大学的神经科学家塞思·格兰特说道，他并未参与这项新研究。
"信息是，从出生到老年，变化是持续不断的。"

sentences: Mousley and her co-authors identified five epochs during which the brain is wired in different ways.
translations: 莫斯利及其合著者确定了大脑以不同方式连接的五个时期。

sentences: From infancy to nine years old, the brain is busy.
There is a lot of consolidation of neural connections, competitive elimination of synapses and rapid increases in gray and white matter.
But the brain is becoming less efficient during this time — so it takes longer for information to get from one region to another.
translations: 从婴儿期到九岁，大脑一直处于忙碌状态。
神经连接大量巩固，突触竞争性消除，灰质和白质迅速增加。
但在此期间，大脑的效率反而降低——因此信息从一个区域传递到另一个区域所需的时间更长。

sentences: "We know that in very early life, the brain makes more connections than it needs, and then it prunes them away," Mousley said.
translations: “我们知道，在生命早期，大脑会建立比所需更多的连接，然后将其修剪掉，”莫斯利说道。

sentences: Whatever the reason, it is a time when a lot of learning happens — language, motor skills, speech — and there is likely a reason the brain is structured this way.
"It could be that this decreasing efficiency is potentially related to this incredible moment of learning," Mousley said.
translations: 无论原因如何，这是一个大量学习发生的时期——语言、运动技能、言语——而且大脑以这种方式构造很可能是有原因的。
“这种效率下降可能与此惊人的学习时刻有关，”莫斯利说。

sentences: There is a dramatic turning point around the age of nine on average — a time when many children begin to enter puberty.
The brain switches gears and starts rewiring to become more efficient.
translations: 平均而言，大约在九岁左右会出现一个戏剧性的转折点——这是许多孩子开始进入青春期的时期。
大脑会切换模式，开始重新连接以变得更高效。

sentences: The adolescence phase lasts into the early 30s on average.
"It is really important to think about adolescence as this protracted window," said Katie Insel, a psychologist at Northwestern University.
This research adds to work suggesting that the brain isn't fully developed or stable until the late 20s or early 30s.
"Something that sets us apart as humans from other animals is how slowly we develop," Mousley said.
translations: 青春期阶段平均持续到30岁出头。
"将青春期视为一个延长的窗口期非常重要，"西北大学心理学家凯蒂·因塞尔说。
这项研究进一步证实了大脑直到20多岁末或30岁出头才完全发育或稳定的观点。
"人类与其他动物不同之处在于我们发育得有多缓慢，"穆斯利说。

sentences: Adulthood is the longest phase — lasting more than three decades from around 32 until around 66 years old.
"It does seem to be this kind of period of relative stability," Mousley said.
"It's consistent for a very long period of time."
That doesn't mean the brain isn't changing, but the changes are less dramatic than in other phases.
"If you think about what an adult is compared to a teenager, you assume a level of stability in behavior.
That's aligning with this three-decade period," Mousley said.
translations: 成年期是最长的阶段——从大约32岁持续到大约66岁，历时三十多年。
"这似乎确实是一个相对稳定的时期，"莫斯利说。
"它在很长一段时间内保持一致。"
这并不意味着大脑没有变化，只是变化不如其他阶段那么显著。
"如果你将成年人与青少年进行比较，你会认为行为上存在一定程度的稳定性。
这与这三十年时期是一致的，"莫斯利说。

sentences: Around 66 years old, the researchers saw another turning point.
This is a time when the brain becomes more vulnerable to age-related diseases — but the news isn't all bad.
"There's an expected and healthy, typical way for the brain to shift," Mousley said.
"There are pros and cons to every developmental stage," Insel said.
"With every phase of life, there are trade-offs."
translations: 在大约66岁时，研究人员观察到了另一个转折点。
这是一个大脑更容易受到与年龄相关疾病影响的时期——但消息并非全是坏消息。
“大脑有一种预期且健康的典型转变方式，”莫斯利说。
“每个发展阶段都有利弊，”因塞尔说。
“人生的每个阶段都有取舍。”

sentences: From 83 onward, the researchers identified a "late aging" phase.
"What we're seeing is something called 'increasing centrality,'" Mousley said.
Particular regions of the brain become more important.
There is reduced connectivity, but there seems to be a pattern to that change.
translations: 从83岁开始，研究人员识别出一个“晚年衰老”阶段。
“我们观察到的是所谓的‘中心性增强’现象，”莫斯利说道。
大脑的特定区域变得更加重要。
连接性有所降低，但这种变化似乎存在某种规律。

sentences: The metaphor Mousley used was that of changing bus routes: If your direct bus stopped running and you had to take two buses, the transfer station would become very important.
She theorized that the brain might be prioritizing important connections if others drop off.
translations: 莫斯利使用的比喻是更换公交路线：如果你的直达公交车停运了，不得不换乘两辆公交车，那么换乘站就会变得非常重要。
她推测，如果其他连接减弱，大脑可能会优先处理重要的连接。

sentences: The word "development" is often associated with childhood or adolescence — but this research shows that the brain develops continually throughout our lives.
translations: “发展”这个词通常与童年或青春期相关联——但这项研究表明，大脑在我们的一生中持续发展。

sentences: "We often ascribe certain brain changes to negative outcomes in adulthood or later life," Insel said.
"But there are certain cognitive features that can be really helpful in aging."
By looking at how the brain changes over the lifespan, Insel hopes we can better understand why our brains might be more vulnerable to certain disorders in adolescence or older age.
translations: "我们常将某些大脑变化归因于成年或晚年生活中的负面结果，" 因塞尔说道。
"但有些认知特征在衰老过程中可能非常有益。"
通过观察大脑在整个生命周期中的变化，因塞尔希望我们能更好地理解为什么大脑在青春期或老年期可能更容易受到某些疾病的影响。

sentences: Yaakov Stern, a neuroscientist at Columbia University, noted that a good next step would be understanding exactly how these measures of the brain might be related to cognitive processes.
He added that many things affecting brain development are within our control — such as diet, exercise and social connection.
"The brain changes with aging.
We know that," Stern said.
"What interests me is whether there are exposures that seem to be associated with more successful aging."
translations: 哥伦比亚大学的神经科学家雅科夫·斯特恩指出，下一步的关键是确切理解这些大脑测量指标如何与认知过程相关联。
他补充说，许多影响大脑发育的因素都在我们的掌控之中——比如饮食、运动和社交联系。
"大脑会随着年龄增长而变化。
我们知道这一点，"斯特恩说。
"我感兴趣的是，是否存在某些因素与更成功的衰老过程相关。"
